chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Alawi, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'From the honor (mur'uah) of a man is that his mounts/beasts be plump (siman)'.

He (the narrator) said, 'And I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Three (things) are from the honor: the agility of the animal, and the beauty of the face of the slave, and the enjoyable mattress (fursh al-sari)'.

key_terms.الْفَرْشُ السَّرِيُّ: The bedding or mattress, often implying comfort or luxury
key_terms.سِمَاناً: Plump, well-fed, or in good condition (referring to beasts of burden)
key_terms.مُرُوءَة: Manly honor, chivalry, or noble character traits

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of muru'ah (honor/chivalry) according to Imam Al-Reza (AS)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) defines 'mur'uah' not merely as moral virtue but as a holistic standard of dignified presentation, linking external appearance to internal character. The inclusion of 'husn wajh al-mamluk' (beauty of the slave/servant) and 'al-farsh al-sari' (fine bedding) reflects the socio-economic context of the time, where material provision and aesthetic care were seen as extensions of a man's honor and capability. This perspective highlights the Shia scholarly view that outward elegance, when free from arrogance, complements inner piety and social responsibility.
